nodes.label: Body
nodes.description: Generic adult body proper. Illustrative procedural figure, not a patient scan.

nodes.label: Head
nodes.description: The head is the anterior-most division of the body [GO].

nodes.label: Face
nodes.description: Front of the head. Uberon has UBERON:0001456 (face); Agent 1 bound the mesh to this DIAMOND id, so the API keeps it for interop.

nodes.label: Neck
nodes.description: An organism subdivision that extends from the head to the pectoral girdle, encompassing the cervical vertebral column.

nodes.label: Thorax
nodes.description: Subdivision of trunk that lies between the head and the abdomen.

nodes.label: Abdomen
nodes.description: The subdivision of the vertebrate body between the thorax and pelvis. The ventral part of the abdomen contains the abdominal cavity and visceral organs. The dorsal part includes the abdominal section of the vertebral column.

nodes.label: Pelvis
nodes.description: The lower segment of the trunk, inferioposterior to the abdomen proper, in the transition area between the trunk and the lower limbs.

nodes.label: Back / spine
nodes.description: Subdivision of skeletal system that consists of all the vertebra and associated skeletal elements and joints in the body[modified from VSAO].

nodes.label: Left arm
nodes.description: A (free) limb that is connected to a pectoral girdle. The extent of this structure includes autopod, stylopod and zeugopod regions when present, but excludes the pectoral girdle and its parts.

nodes.label: Right arm
nodes.description: A (free) limb that is connected to a pectoral girdle. The extent of this structure includes autopod, stylopod and zeugopod regions when present, but excludes the pectoral girdle and its parts.

nodes.label: Left shoulder
nodes.description: A subdivision of the pectoral complex consisting of the structures in the region of the shoulder joint (which connects the humerus, scapula and clavicle).

nodes.label: Right shoulder
nodes.description: A subdivision of the pectoral complex consisting of the structures in the region of the shoulder joint (which connects the humerus, scapula and clavicle).

nodes.label: Left upper arm
synonyms: proximal segment of free upper limb
nodes.description: The part of the forelimb between pectoral region and the elbow, corresponding to the humerus.

nodes.label: Right upper arm
synonyms: proximal segment of free upper limb
nodes.description: The part of the forelimb between pectoral region and the elbow, corresponding to the humerus.

nodes.label: Left forearm
synonyms: intermediate segment of free upper limb
nodes.description: The middle limb segment of the pectoral free limb, between the autopod and stylopod segments. Includes as parts the forelimb zeugopodial skeleton, which includes as parts the radius and ulna, or their cartilage precursors, or evolutionary variants.

nodes.label: Right forearm
synonyms: intermediate segment of free upper limb
nodes.description: The middle limb segment of the pectoral free limb, between the autopod and stylopod segments. Includes as parts the forelimb zeugopodial skeleton, which includes as parts the radius and ulna, or their cartilage precursors, or evolutionary variants.

nodes.label: Left hand
synonyms: terminal segment of free upper limb
nodes.description: Distal segment of the fore limb, including carpal region, metacarpal region and digits.

nodes.label: Right hand
synonyms: terminal segment of free upper limb
nodes.description: Distal segment of the fore limb, including carpal region, metacarpal region and digits.

nodes.label: Left leg
nodes.description: A (free) limb that is connected to a pelvic girdle region. The extent of this structure includes autopod, stylopod and zeugopod regions when present, but excludes the pelvic girdle and its parts.

nodes.label: Right leg
nodes.description: A (free) limb that is connected to a pelvic girdle region. The extent of this structure includes autopod, stylopod and zeugopod regions when present, but excludes the pelvic girdle and its parts.

nodes.label: Left thigh
synonyms: proximal segment of free lower limb
nodes.description: The part of the hindlimb between pelvis and the knee, corresponding to the femur.

nodes.label: Right thigh
synonyms: proximal segment of free lower limb
nodes.description: The part of the hindlimb between pelvis and the knee, corresponding to the femur.

nodes.label: Left lower leg
synonyms: intermediate segment of free lower limb
nodes.description: The middle limb segment of the pelvic free limb, between the autopod and stylopod segments. Includes as parts the hindlimb zeugopodial skeleton, which includes as parts the tibia and fibula, or their cartilage precursors, or evolutionary variants.

nodes.label: Right lower leg
synonyms: intermediate segment of free lower limb
nodes.description: The middle limb segment of the pelvic free limb, between the autopod and stylopod segments. Includes as parts the hindlimb zeugopodial skeleton, which includes as parts the tibia and fibula, or their cartilage precursors, or evolutionary variants.

nodes.label: Left foot
synonyms: terminal segment of free lower limb
nodes.description: Distal portion of the hind limb, including tarsal region, metatarsal region and digits.

nodes.label: Right foot
synonyms: terminal segment of free lower limb
nodes.description: Distal portion of the hind limb, including tarsal region, metatarsal region and digits.

nodes.label: Brain
nodes.description: The brain is the center of the nervous system in all vertebrate, and most invertebrate, animals. Some primitive animals such as jellyfish and starfish have a decentralized nervous system without a brain, while sponges lack any nervous system at all. In vertebrates, the brain is located in the head, protected by the skull and close to the primary sensory apparatus of vision, hearing, balance, taste, and smell[WP].

nodes.label: Left eye
nodes.description: An eye that is part of a left side of organism [Automatically generated definition].

nodes.label: Right eye
nodes.description: An eye that is part of a right side of organism [Automatically generated definition].

nodes.label: Left ear
nodes.description: The organ of hearing located on the left side of the head[ncit,modified].

nodes.label: Right ear
nodes.description: The organ of hearing located on the right side of the head.

nodes.label: Nose
nodes.description: The olfactory organ of vertebrates, consisting of nares, olfactory epithelia and the structures and skeletal framework of the nasal cavity.

nodes.label: Mouth
nodes.description: The proximal portion of the digestive tract, containing the oral cavity and bounded by the oral opening. In vertebrates, this extends to the pharynx and includes gums, lips, tongue and parts of the palate. Typically also includes the teeth, except where these occur elsewhere (e.g. pharyngeal jaws) or protrude from the mouth (tusks).

nodes.label: Heart
nodes.description: Taxon notes:" the ascidian tube-like heart lacks chambers....The ascidian heart is formed after metamorphosis as a simple tube-like structure with a single-layered myoepithelium that is continuous with a single-layered pericar- dial wall. It lacks chambers and endocardium.... The innovation of the chambered heart was a key event in vertebrate evolution, because the chambered heart generates one-way blood flow with high pressure, a critical requirement for the efficient blood supply of large-body vertebrates... all extant vertebrates have hearts with two or more chambers (Moorman and Christoffels 2003)" DOI:10.1101/gad.1485706

nodes.label: Left lung
nodes.description: Lung which consists of the left upper lobe and left lower lobe.[FMA].

nodes.label: Right lung
nodes.description: Lung which consists of the right upper lobe, middle lobe and right lower lobe.[FMA].

nodes.label: Liver
nodes.description: An exocrine gland which secretes bile and functions in metabolism of protein and carbohydrate and fat, synthesizes substances involved in the clotting of the blood, synthesizes vitamin A, detoxifies poisonous substances, stores glycogen, and breaks down worn-out erythrocytes[GO].

nodes.label: Stomach
nodes.description: An expanded region of the vertebrate alimentary tract that serves as a food storage compartment and digestive organ. A stomach is lined, in whole or in part by a glandular epithelium.

nodes.label: Pancreas
nodes.description: An endoderm derived structure that produces precursors of digestive enzymes and blood glucose regulating hormones[GO].

nodes.label: Left kidney
nodes.description: A kidney that is part of a left side of organism [Automatically generated definition].

nodes.label: Right kidney
nodes.description: A kidney that is part of a right side of organism [Automatically generated definition].

nodes.label: Bladder
nodes.description: Distensible musculomembranous organ situated in the anterior part of the pelvic cavity in which urine collects before excretion[MP].

nodes.label: Spleen
nodes.description: The organ that functions to filter blood and to store red corpuscles and platelets.

nodes.label: Small intestine
nodes.description: Subdivision of digestive tract that connects the stomach to the large intestine and is where much of the digestion and absorption of food takes place (with the exception of ruminants). The mammalian small intestine is long and coiled and can be differentiated histologically into: duodenum, jejunem, ileum[WP,cjm,Kardong].

nodes.label: Large intestine
nodes.description: A subdivision of the digestive tract that connects the small intestine to the cloaca or anus. Lacks or has few villi[Kardong].

nodes.label: Gallbladder
nodes.description: Rats do not have a gallbladder, but produce bile. The bile flows directly from the liver through the (hepatic) bile duct into the small intestine (Hebel and Stromberg, 1988)

nodes.label: Thyroid
nodes.description: A two-lobed endocrine gland found in all vertebrates, located in front of and on either side of the trachea in humans, and producing various hormones, such as triiodothyronine and calcitonin[BTO].

nodes.label: Larynx
nodes.description: A continuation of the pharynx that is involved in breathing, sound production, and protecting the trachea against food aspiration.

nodes.label: Oesophagus
nodes.description: Tube that connects the pharynx to the stomach. In mammals, the oesophagus connects the buccal cavity with the stomach. The stratified squamous non-keratinised epithelium lining the buccal cavity is continued through the pharynx down into the oesophagus. The lowest part of the oesophagus (ca. 2 cm) is lined with gastric mucosa and covered by peritoneum. The main body of the oesophagus is lined with small, simple mucous glands. Each gland opens into the lumen by a long duct which pierces the muscularis mucosae (Wilson and Washington, 1989). A sphincter is situated at the point where the oesophagus enters the stomach to prevent gastro-oesophageal reflux, i.e. to prevent acidic gastric contents from reaching stratified epithelia of the oesophagus, where they can cause inflammation and irritation (Wilson and Washington, 1989; Brown et al., 1993).

nodes.label: Aorta
nodes.description: The main trunk of the systemic arterial system that carries blood from the heart to all the organs and other structures of the body, bringing oxygenated blood to all parts of the body in the systemic circulation.

nodes.label: Tongue
nodes.description: A muscular organ in the floor of the mouth.

nodes.label: Spinal cord
nodes.description: Part of the central nervous system located in the vertebral canal continuous with and caudal to the brain; demarcated from brain by plane of foramen magnum. It is composed of an inner core of gray matter in which nerve cells predominate, and an outer layer of white matter in which myelinated nerve fibers predominate, and surrounds the central canal. (CUMBO).

nodes.label: Adrenal gland
nodes.description: The thick outer layer of the adrenal gland that produces and secretes steroid hormones such as corticosterone, estrone and aldosterone.

nodes.label: Uterus
nodes.description: The female muscular organ of gestation in which the developing embryo or fetus is nourished until birth.

nodes.label: Prostate
nodes.description: The prostate gland is a partly muscular, partly glandular body that is situated near the base of the mammalian male urethra and secretes an alkaline viscid fluid which is a major constituent of the ejaculatory fluid.

nodes.label: Skin
nodes.description: The organ covering the body that consists of the dermis and epidermis.

nodes.label: Skeletal muscle tissue
nodes.description: Muscle tissue that consists primarily of skeletal muscle fibers.

nodes.label: Bone tissue
nodes.description: Skeletal tissue with a collagen-rich extracellular matrix vascularized, mineralized with hydroxyapatite and typically including osteocytes located in lacunae that communicate with one another by cell processes (in canaliculi). Bone is deposited by osteoblasts.

nodes.label: Neural tissue
nodes.description: Portion of tissue in the nervous system which consists of neurons and glial cells, and may also contain parts of the vasculature.

nodes.label: Connective tissue
nodes.description: Tissue with cells that deposit non-polarized extracellular matrix including connective tissue fibers and ground substance.

nodes.label: Cardiac muscle tissue
nodes.description: Muscle tissue composed of cardiac muscle cells, forming the muscles of the heart[ZFA,modified].

nodes.label: Adipose tissue
nodes.description: Portion of connective tissue composed of adipocytes enmeshed in areolar tissue.

nodes.label: Blood vessel
nodes.description: A vessel through which blood circulates in the body.

nodes.label: Apex of heart
nodes.description: The apex of the heart is the lowest superficial part of the heart. It is directed downward, forward, and to the left, and is overlapped by the left lung and pleura. [WP,unvetted].

nodes.label: Lung
nodes.description: Snakes and limbless lizards typically possess only the right lung as a major respiratory organ; the left lung is greatly reduced, or even absent. Amphisbaenians, however, have the opposite arrangement, with a major left lung, and a reduced or absent right lung [WP]

nodes.label: Kidney
nodes.description: A paired organ of the urinary tract that produces urine and maintains bodily fluid homeostasis, blood pressure, pH levels, red blood cell production and skeleton mineralization.

nodes.label: Cerebral cortex
nodes.description: The thin layer of gray matter on the surface of the cerebral hemisphere that develops from the telencephalon. It consists of the neocortex (6 layered cortex or isocortex), the hippocampal formation and the olfactory cortex.
